title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

findings.explanation: The code uses Django ORM querysets (Project.objects.filter) which utilize parameterized queries internally. There is no raw SQL string concatenation or user-controlled input reaching a SQL query directly.

The change refactors the logic for filtering projects based on team access levels. The new logic correctly handles the cases where `admin` and `member` flags are set. If both are true, it returns all projects the user is a member of (which is the correct behavior for a user with both permissions). If only one is true, it filters by that specific access level. This does not introduce an IDOR or missing authorization flaw; it maintains the existing authorization model by ensuring users only see projects they have access to via their team memberships.
